solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Purge by making bloodsucker first do what it says it does!

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word bloodsucker and puts it at the front

parts.words: do what it says it does
parts.note: a leech drains, and to leach is to drain or wash out, a verb that sounds just like the creature's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation about cleansing something by setting a leech to work on it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes B from 'bloodsucker'; the rest of the clue asks for the action the bloodsucker's name suggests, LEACH, to drain out, which sounds like LEECH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to whiten and cleanse, so it can stand for purging something of colour or stain.

clue.text: Debrett's list has restriction on seniority

parts.note: a bar is a restriction or ban
taken as written
age is seniority in years

explanation.surface: A guide to the aristocracy includes a limit on rank by age.
explanation.walkthrough: Debrett's is the British reference book of the peerage and aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The barons collectively make up the baronage, the class listed in a peerage guide.

clue.text: Sea pigeon tested for intelligence

indicators.note: tested suggests the letters are tried out in a different order

explanation.surface: A seabird is put through trials to measure its brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tested' rearranges SEA PIGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is the gathering of secret information, intelligence in the spying sense.

clue.text: Cover proceedings

definitions.meaning: a box or sheath that encloses something
a legal action brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a protective holder and a lawsuit heard in court.

clue.text: Certify direct transfer to account

parts.note: A/C, often written AC, is the usual abbreviation for account

indicators.note: transfer suggests moving letters about, so the word direct is rearranged

explanation.surface: Banking instructions about sending money straight into an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' looks like part of a banking phrase but signals the anagram of DIRECT; the account abbreviation goes first even though it is printed last.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to officially recognise or vouch for, a synonym of certify.

clue.text: Ceremonial remains

parts.note: sounds like relics or ashes from a rite, but means the paper scraps left after a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: The scattered paper pieces thrown at weddings are what is left after the ceremony.

clue.text: About to barter with bent organisation? In short, that's degenerate

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: with signals that the bent letters sit inside the word for barter

parts.note: to trade is to barter

indicators.note: bent suggests twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: org is short for organisation

explanation.surface: A remark about doing deals with a crooked firm being morally corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' (crooked) signals the anagram of ORG, giving ROG, and 'with' sets it inside the word for barter; the question mark and 'In short' mark the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde as a verb means to go backward or decline, so it can mean degenerate.

clue.text: See 22
Drink endlessly with the French, then walk unsteadily …

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the drink's name

parts.note: a toddy is a hot spirit drink
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone drinks too much in France and then staggers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from TODDY.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short, unsteady steps like a small child.

clue.text: … drunk but happy!

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slightly tipsy and cheerful, as in festive greetings.

clue.text: Priest has nothing prepared as an answer

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A clergyman has no ready reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges PRIEST plus O into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a kind of answer.

clue.text: Marked those cakes that weren't decorated

definitions.meaning: marked here means observed or spotted
cakes left plain were ..., written as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have marked or observed it.

clue.text: Element No. 10 has gone on to embrace

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold within, so the answer sits inside the words gone on

explanation.surface: A tenth element has gone on to hug someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' points to the letters running across 'goNE ON'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is the chemical element with atomic number ten.

clue.text: No-one charges to see this contest!

definitions.text: No-one charges to see this contest!

parts.words: No-one charges to see this contest!
parts.note: read as a show with free entry for everybody, but the phrase also names a chaotic brawl where anyone joins in

explanation.definitionFit: A disorganised fight or contest that anyone may join is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Fresh information for consumers

parts.note: reads like news for the public, but is the label telling shoppers how long food stays fresh

explanation.definitionFit: A label on food telling shoppers the last day it should be sold while still fresh.

clue.text: Old cricketer with degree is honoured

parts.note: W G Grace was the great Victorian English cricketer

explanation.surface: A veteran cricketer holding a university degree receives an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: W G GRACE was a famous English cricketer of the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: To be graced is to be honoured or dignified by something.

clue.text: It's more obvious when nearly naked

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for naked is dropped

parts.note: starkers is British slang for stark naked

explanation.surface: Something shows up more clearly when one is almost undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for naked; 'nearly' drops its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means plain or unmistakable, so its comparative means more plainly evident.

clue.text: Cures Noel with restorative compound

indicators.note: restorative suggests putting back into a new state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A healing compound restores a man named Noel to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restorative' rearranges CURES NOEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is a fenced compound or yard.

clue.text: Seize control of large part of Yorkshire town

indicators.note: large part of means nearly all, so the first letter of the town is dropped

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Taking over most of a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROGATE is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England; 'large part of' drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or take something without right, a synonym of seizing control.

clue.text: Barrister discards note, but gives thanks in return for drink

indicators.note: discards means throws out, so the note is removed from the barrister's title

parts.note: an advocate is a barrister, especially in Scotland
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in return means the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A lawyer skips a note but offers thanks for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discards' removes TE from ADVOCATE; 'in return' turns TA into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs and brandy, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Announce a month of real change

parts.note: Dec is short for December

indicators.note: change asks for the letters of real to be altered in order

explanation.surface: Making a proclamation about a month of genuine reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' signals the anagram of REAL; 'month of real change' reads as a political slogan rather than a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to state openly or proclaim, a synonym of announce.

clue.text: Beheaded, cut down and drawn out

indicators.note: beheaded means the top or first letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: reduced means cut down or lessened

explanation.surface: A grim list of executions: beheaded, felled and drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' removes the R from REDUCED; the surface evokes hanging, drawing and quartering.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or elicit, so the past participle means drawn out.

clue.text: Piece in erotic ad provoked comments from the judge

indicators.note: in means the piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
provoked suggests stirred up, so the letters of erotic ad are rearranged

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A section of a racy advert drew remarks from the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provoked' rearranges EROTIC AD into OERDICTA; 'in' puts BIT inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dicta are incidental remarks made by a judge that are not binding.

clue.text: Eastern European heads north to escape

indicators.note: heads north in a down clue means the pieces are read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: An Eastern European travels north to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads north' reverses E plus POLE, giving ELOPE when read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry, so it means escape.

clue.text: Best mate's meeting a girl? That'll be the day, he noted

definitions.text: That'll be the day, he noted

parts.note: a buddy is a close friend; the possessive adds no letter
Holly is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man's best friend has a date with a girl, prompting a sceptical retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That'll Be the Day' was a 1957 hit by the American rock and roll singer; 'noted' means sang.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer recorded the song That'll Be the Day, so he is the one who noted it in song.

clue.text: Risked getting the chop!

definitions.meaning: gambled, as in dicing with death

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gambled with fate and cut into small cubes.

clue.text: Perform trick, one that hasn't been seen for years!

definitions.text: one that hasn't been seen for years

parts.note: to do something is to perform it
a do is a swindle or trick, as in to do someone

explanation.surface: A magician performs a vanishing act not seen in ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless Mauritian bird became extinct in the 1600s, so it has not been seen for centuries.

clue.text: Hasn't even paid chap for print measure

indicators.note: lacking the even letters means only the odd-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: A man has not been paid in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't even' keeps the odd letters of 'paid chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pica is a typographic unit of twelve points, a measure used in printing.

clue.text: Work to get animal into ill-fitting coat

indicators.note: into places the animal inside the rearranged letters of coat
ill-fitting suggests the coat is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Trying to squeeze a pet into a coat that doesn't fit takes some effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-fitting' signals the anagram of COAT, giving TOCA, and 'into' houses the animal; 'Work' is a musical composition, not effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a musical work, typically a showy keyboard piece.

clue.text: Dug up pelargonium; gone out to get another flower

indicators.note: dug up suggests the plant's letters are turned over and rearranged, with those of gone taken out

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts a dead geranium and plants something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G, O, N, E from PELARGONIUM ('gone out') and rearrange what is left ('Dug up').
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a flowering plant, the genus including primroses, as a pelargonium is also a flower.

clue.text: As river enters the sea, setter is in need of being rescued

indicators.note: enters means the river goes inside the name for the sea
is in says the setter also goes inside the sea, following the river

parts.note: the Red Sea, so the sea here is RED
the Dee is a river in Britain
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Where a river runs into the sea, the compiler is stranded and needs saving.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'enters' and 'is in' put pieces inside RED, the Red Sea; the DEE is a river in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be redeemed is to be saved or delivered, a synonym of rescued.

clue.text: Officer has the last word in requiem

indicators.note: has means the officer holds the other word inside him

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

explanation.surface: A military officer gets the final say at a funeral mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' signals that the officer holds the closing word of a prayer; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a song of mourning, as a requiem is music for the dead.
